headline: Foreign buyers return and Daimler leads the rebound
text: German share indices rose about 10% in less than three weeks in February as foreign investors stopped selling and began to buy again, followed by German insurers. The dollar has stabilised and interest rates are falling. Reports say Daimler-Benz is close to taking over the aerospace and defence group MBB, as the federal government wants.
source: Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Aktien wieder hoffähig', 19 February 1988, https://www.zeit.de/1988/08/aktien-wieder-hoffaehig (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Markt-Report: Ein Lichtblick', 12 February 1988, https://www.zeit.de/1988/07/ein-lichtblick (read 2026-10-03); Die Zeit, 'Daimler/MBB: Perversion', 12 February 1988, https://www.zeit.de/1988/07/perversion (read 2026-10-03)

headline: Missiles on Tehran, poison gas on Halabja
text: Iraq has been firing long-range missiles at Tehran and other cities in a new 'war of the cities'. On 16 March Iraqi aircraft dropped chemical weapons on the Kurdish town of Halabja, which Iranian forces had just entered. Journalists brought in by Iran found streets of dead families; Iran says thousands of civilians were killed. Western reaction has been muted.
imageCaption: Iranian soldiers at the front during the Iran-Iraq war

headline: The 10,000th McDonald's
text: McDonald's opened its 10,000th restaurant in April, 33 years after Ray Kroc's first. Outside the United States its strongest markets are Japan, Canada, Germany, Britain, Australia and France. On 29 April McDonald's Canada signed a joint-venture agreement with Moscow city officials to open 20 restaurants in the Soviet capital, the first one due in late 1989.
imageCaption: McDonald's roadside sign with the golden arches

headline: Nestlé wins Rowntree for £2.55 billion
text: Nestlé won the battle for Rowntree, the British maker of Kit Kat, After Eight and Smarties, with an offer valuing it at £2.55 billion. The fight began on 13 April, when the Zurich chocolate firm Jacobs Suchard bought 14.9% of Rowntree in a dawn raid and Nestlé offered itself as a protective buyer. Rowntree is the world's fourth-largest chocolate maker; critics in Britain point out that Swiss rules protect Nestlé itself from such a takeover.
imageCaption: The Rowntree factory in York, England

headline: Khomeini accepts a ceasefire: 'more deadly than poison'
text: Iran said in mid-July that it accepts Resolution 598 and a ceasefire with Iraq. Ayatollah Khomeini said that accepting it was 'more deadly than drinking from a poisoned chalice'. UN observers are to supervise the truce. The war has lasted almost eight years; the dead are counted in the hundreds of thousands.
imageCaption: Ayatollah Khomeini at his residence in Jamaran, Tehran

headline: Philip Morris buys Kraft for 13.1 billion dollars
text: On 30 October Kraft agreed to be bought by Philip Morris for 106 dollars a share, about 13.1 billion dollars, after Philip Morris raised its hostile offer from 90 dollars. It is the second-largest takeover in US history and makes Philip Morris the world's largest consumer goods company, with Kraft cheese, Philadelphia cream cheese and Velveeta next to General Foods' brands.

headline: Nestlé opens its registered share to foreigners; the bearer share tumbles
text: On 17 November Nestlé's board decided that foreigners may now hold its registered shares, which until now only Swiss investors could own and which traded at about half the price of the bearer share. The registered share rose from 4,375 to 6,000 francs in November, while the bearer share, until now the only class open to foreigners, fell from 8,890 to 6,875. Bearer shares of other Swiss companies fell too.
source: NZZ prices of 31 Oct and 30 Nov 1988 in data/manual/raw/nzz-notes-1988.md (from scan NZZ_1988-12-01.pdf p. 41, read 2026-10-03); Loderer and Jacobs, 'The Nestlé crash', Journal of Financial Economics 37(3), 1995, abstract via search result summary (read 2026-10-03)

headline: George Bush wins the White House: "Read my lips, no new taxes"
text: Vice President George Bush won the presidency on 8 November with 426 electoral votes and 53.4% of the vote against Michael Dukakis, the governor of Massachusetts. The campaign was marked by Bush's convention pledge, "Read my lips: no new taxes", and for Dukakis's ride in a tank, which the Bush campaign turned into an attack advertisement. Bush takes over from Reagan in January with the economy in its sixth year of growth.
imageCaption: George Bush watches the election returns in Houston, 8 November 1988

headline: Nikkei passes 30,000
text: Tokyo's Nikkei 225 passed 30,000 in December and ended the year at 30,159, up from 21,564 a year earlier. The dollar buys about 124 yen, half of what it bought before the Plaza agreement. Japan's banks are now the biggest in the world by assets and stock market value.
